scope.goal: Adopt Kafka as the canonical broker, make producer ownership normative, demonstrate an atomic Inventory reservation source outbox, correct two Inventory event field names, and harden the source-independent reconstruction gate.
scope.target: Inventory ReserveInventory application/infrastructure slice, Inventory integration contracts, SQL/runtime configuration, focused tests, and reconstruction specifications
constraints: Kafka is the canonical runtime path and ProductId is the Inventory ordering partition key.
The producer owns integration-event meaning and schema; consumers own only their reactions and delivery handling.
ReserveInventory stock mutation, terminal outcome, and source-outbox insert must commit or roll back together.
External-service tests remain opt-in and skipped results are never counted as passing evidence.
RabbitMQ remains a deferred compatibility profile; no fanout topology is claimed or implemented in this slice.
non_goals: Convert IncreaseStock, DecreaseStock, or Restock to the source-outbox pattern.
Implement RabbitMQ exchange or per-consumer queue topology.
Delete source, push, open a pull request, merge, close Issue #2, or publish.

architecture_decisions: Kafka is canonical for event-driven verification and per-product ordering.
The producing bounded context owns integration-event meaning and schema.
ReserveInventory uses an explicit application transaction port and a PostgreSQL source outbox.
user_constraints: Adopt the recommendations provisionally so the owner can inspect the actual code architecture and adjust later.
Keep RabbitMQ available for future broadcast evaluation or dual deployment.
Use a strict reconstruction gate provisionally and adjust it from observed results.

approval_contract.required_before: production architecture, specification, contract, SQL, runtime configuration, and test changes

finding_evidence: Direct publish occurs after PostgresInventoryReservationRepository commits.
acceptance_criteria: ReserveInventoryUseCase creates the producer-owned integration event and supplies stable MessageId and ProductId partition key before commit.
PostgreSQL commits reservation state, terminal outcome, and source-outbox row atomically.
A bounded relay retries with stable delivery metadata, retains publication evidence, and parks after five failed attempts.
Increase and return event quantity fields use their correct names in code, tests, and reconstruction contracts.
Kafka, RabbitMQ, producer ownership, and strict reconstruction gates are documented without claiming unverified runtime behavior.

applicability.reason: Atomic Inventory source-outbox and relay implementation.

selection.reason: One overlapping mutation scope; delegated agents were not requested.

applicability.reason: Transaction, relay, and contract behavior require executable GWT oracles.

selection.reason: Tests overlap the same production/specification integration scope.

applicability.reason: The slice enables one existing OutboxRelay flag but does not introduce a new environment/profile model.

selection.reason: Existing Messaging configuration contract remains unchanged.

steps: Record the broker, ownership, transactional-outbox, contract-correction, and reconstruction-gate decisions.
Introduce an explicit Inventory reservation transaction port owned by Application.
Implement PostgreSQL atomic reservation/outbox persistence and a stable-identity relay.
Correct Inventory increase/return quantity contract names and all call-site assertions.
Run focused build/tests, parse/spec/workflow validation, and the unchanged compliance gate.
validation: Broker-free Inventory tests pass by default.
External PostgreSQL tests remain skipped without opt-in and prove outbox atomicity when run.
Inventory and dependent Orders tests compile and pass.
JSON/YAML/workflow/spec validators pass; unavailable external evidence remains non-passing.
execution.commit_checkpoint: Kafka ownership, Inventory reservation source outbox, corrected event contracts, and reconstruction gate checkpoint.
deferred_items: RabbitMQ broadcast topology and dual-deployment decision.
Source-outbox adoption for other Inventory commands.
Outbox retention/archival policy after production observation.
Final owner acceptance of the concrete transaction-port design.

approval_evidence: User decisions on 2026-08-27 and GitHub Issue #2.
